sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: When the images from the James Webb telescope were revealed, my reaction was just slack-jawed wonder.
sentences.zh: 当詹姆斯·韦伯望远镜拍摄的图像公布时，我的反应只有目瞪口呆的惊叹。

sentences.en: It's this Christmas of stars.
sentences.zh: 这简直是群星的圣诞节。

sentences.en: We see these brilliant points of light and pinwheels of distant galaxies and stellar nurseries, these locations where clouds of collapsing gas and dust give birth to stars.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这些璀璨的光点、遥远星系的旋涡和恒星托儿所，也就是那些坍缩的气体和尘埃云孕育恒星的地方。

sentences.en: Seeing the images is like seeing a painting in your mind that suddenly doesn't look
sentences.zh: 看到这些图像，就像在脑海中看到一幅画，它突然看起来不再

sentences.en: fuzzy anymore, like so many pictures of stars we've seen in the paSt. So do you remember those beautiful vertical streaks of gas?
sentences.zh: 模糊了，不像我们过去看到的那么多恒星照片。还记得那些美丽的垂直气体条纹吗？

sentences.en: They were in that first set of images.
sentences.zh: 它们就在第一批图像中。

sentences.en: They look like mountains, big, auburn, and gold.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来像山脉，宏伟、赤褐且金黄。

sentences.en: NASA called them cosmic cliffs.
sentences.zh: NASA 将其称为“宇宙悬崖”。

sentences.en: They were said to be four light years high.
sentences.zh: 据说它们有四光年高。

sentences.en: I did some quick math, and that works out to about 24 trillion miles.
sentences.zh: 我简单算了一下，那大约是 24 万亿英里。

sentences.en: And that made me think, well, we can look at these images aesthetically with wonder, but we could also look at them with total confusion.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，好吧，我们可以从美学角度惊叹地欣赏这些图像，但我们也可以带着彻底的困惑来看待它们。

sentences.en: What do we make of that scale?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何理解这种规模？

sentences.en: What do we make of our lives and our place in this universe?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何理解我们的生活以及我们在宇宙中的位置？

sentences.en: My name is John Gertner, and I'm a contributing writer for the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫约翰·格特纳，是《纽约时报》杂志的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: We've been looking for signs of life in the universe for at least a half a century.
sentences.zh: 至少半个世纪以来，我们一直在寻找宇宙中存在生命的迹象。

sentences.en: And for many years, that search has focused on using radio astronomy.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这种搜索一直集中在射电天文学上。

sentences.en: We tried pulling signals out of the sky that would hint at somebody out there who's trying to communicate with us.
sentences.zh: 我们试图从天空中捕捉那些暗示有外星生命正试图与我们交流的信号。

sentences.en: We've never found anything.
sentences.zh: 但我们从未发现任何东西。

sentences.en: But over the last couple of decades, there's been a kind of two-part revolution in astronomy.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几十年里，天文学领域发生了一场两阶段的革命。

sentences.en: We've discovered all these exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了所有这些系外行星。

sentences.en: These are planets orbiting around distant stars.
sentences.zh: 这些是围绕遥远恒星运行的行星。

sentences.en: And by now, NASA has discovered more than 5,000 of them.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，NASA 已经发现了 5000 多颗。

sentences.en: Each one is a place to look for life.
sentences.zh: 每一颗都是寻找生命的地方。

sentences.en: We also now have this new arsenal of tools, like the Webb Telescope, which can look at atmospheres around these exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还拥有了一套新的工具库，比如韦伯望远镜，它可以观测这些系外行星周围的大气层。

sentences.en: So I wrote about this team of scientists who, rather than scanning radio signals, think mostly about what in those atmospheres might give away that there is life on a planet.
sentences.zh: 所以我写了一篇关于这个科学家团队的文章，他们不再扫描无线电信号，而是主要思考大气层中什么迹象可能表明行星上存在生命。

sentences.en: The scientists catalog these signs as technosignatures.
sentences.zh: 科学家们将这些迹象归类为“技术签名”。

sentences.en: Technosignatures are not just indications that there's life, like the way you would see with slime mold or algae.
sentences.zh: 技术签名不仅仅是存在生命的迹象，就像你看到的黏菌或藻类那样。

sentences.en: They would be indications of a sophisticated society or civilization.
sentences.zh: 它们是复杂社会或文明的迹象。

sentences.en: It could be a mark of some kind of industry or of agriculture.
sentences.zh: 它可能是某种工业或农业的痕迹。

sentences.en: It would be something that's not explainable by natural phenomena.
sentences.zh: 它将是无法用自然现象解释的东西。

sentences.en: Pollution is a really good example of a technosignature.
sentences.zh: 污染就是一个很好的技术签名例子。

sentences.en: There's a certain class of chemicals, like chlorofluorocarbons or CFCs, that are industrial byproducts.
sentences.zh: 有一类化学物质，比如氯氟烃或 CFCs，它们是工业副产品。

sentences.en: Nitrogen dioxide is another one.
sentences.zh: 二氧化氮是另一种。

sentences.en: They would have astronomers wondering what natural process would allow for the formation of that.
sentences.zh: 它们会让天文学家好奇，什么样的自然过程会导致它们的形成。

sentences.en: And if that can't be explained, then maybe there's some kind of society doing something there.
sentences.zh: 如果无法解释，那么可能就是某种社会在那里做了什么。

sentences.en: Technosignatures might give us an understanding of our own culture and our own civilization, too.
sentences.zh: 技术签名也可能让我们了解我们自己的文化和文明。

sentences.en: Say we don't find any technosignatures, like maybe technologically sophisticated societies tend to self-destruct.
sentences.zh: 假设我们没有发现任何技术签名，也许是因为技术先进的社会往往会自我毁灭。

sentences.en: And that'd only be a warning that what we're doing with our own technologies is dangerous and maybe fatal.
sentences.zh: 那只会是一个警告，说明我们对自己技术的使用是危险的，甚至是致命的。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I think we can't be looking for beings exactly like ourselves either.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我认为我们也不能只寻找和我们完全一样的生物。

sentences.en: I mean, not just biologically, but also temperamentally as conquerors, as resource-consuming planet wreckers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是在生物学上，而且在性格上，作为征服者，作为消耗资源的行星破坏者。

sentences.en: We have to think more expansively about what a society can be.
sentences.zh: 我们必须更广阔地思考一个社会可以是什么样子。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it be possible for a society to have advanced technology, but also be totally in balance with its planet?
sentences.zh: 一个社会难道不能拥有先进的技术，同时又与它的行星完全平衡吗？

sentences.en: So the idea that we should put a lot of resources into looking for life beyond Earth has fallen out of favor over the years.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们应该投入大量资源寻找地球以外生命的观点，这些年来已经不再受青睐了。

sentences.en: One of the main characters in my story talks about the giggle factor, which is what anyone who searches for extraterrestrials inevitably encounters.
sentences.zh: 我故事中的一位主角谈到了“傻笑因素”，这是任何寻找外星人的人不可避免会遇到的情况。

sentences.en: But I think there was a time when we were much, much more open to the idea that life existed out there and that we would find it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为曾经有一段时间，我们对生命存在于那里并且我们会找到它的想法要开放得多。

sentences.en: I can't predict the future, but with these new tools and new ways of going about our search, it does seem like a much better
sentences.zh: 我无法预测未来，但随着这些新工具和寻找方法，这似乎是一个更好的

sentences.en: time to be looking up and saying, maybe, maybe we will find something.
sentences.zh: 抬头仰望并说，也许，也许我们会发现什么的时刻。

sentences.en: When the space shuttle Atlantis lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center on October 18th, 1989, it carried the Galileo in its cargo bay.
sentences.zh: 1989年10月18日，当亚特兰蒂斯号航天飞机从肯尼迪航天中心升空时，它的货舱里载着伽利略号探测器。

sentences.en: Arrayed with scientific instruments, Galileo's ultimate destination was Jupiter, where it would spend years in orbit collecting data and taking pictures.
sentences.zh: 伽利略号配备了科学仪器，其最终目的地是木星，它将在那里绕轨道运行多年，收集数据并拍摄照片。

sentences.en: After it left the shuttle, though,
sentences.zh: 不过，在离开航天飞机后，

sentences.en: Galileo headed in the other direction, turning toward the Sun and circling around Venus in order to
sentences.zh: 伽利略号向另一个方向前进，转向太阳并绕金星飞行，以便

sentences.en: slingshot around the planet and pick up speed for its journey to the outer solar system.
sentences.zh: 利用行星引力弹弓效应加速，开启前往外太阳系的旅程。

sentences.en: Along the way, it flew around Earth too.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，它也绕地球飞行。

sentences.en: Twice, in fact, at altitudes of 597 and 188 miles.
sentences.zh: 事实上是两次，高度分别为 597 英里和 188 英里。

sentences.en: This gave its engineering team an opportunity to test the craft's sensors.
sentences.zh: 这让工程团队有机会测试探测器的传感器。

sentences.en: The astronomer Carl Sagan, a member of
sentences.zh: 天文学家卡尔·萨根，作为

sentences.en: Galileo's science team, called the maneuver the first flyby in our planet's history.
sentences.zh: 伽利略号科学团队的一员，称这次机动为我们行星历史上第一次飞越。

sentences.en: It also allowed him to contemplate what a spacecraft might find when looking at a far-off planet for signs of intelligent life.
sentences.zh: 这也让他得以思考，当航天器观察遥远行星寻找智慧生命迹象时，可能会发现什么。

sentences.en: There was plenty to see.
sentences.zh: 有很多东西可以看到。

sentences.en: Our technology creates an intriguing mess.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术创造了一团令人着迷的混乱。

sentences.en: Lights blaze, and heat islands glow in paved-over urban areas.
sentences.zh: 灯火辉煌，热岛在铺设好的城市区域闪烁。

sentences.en: Atmospheric gases ebb and flow, evident today not only in rising concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane, but also in clouds of floating industrial byproducts.
sentences.zh: 大气气体起伏不定，如今不仅体现在二氧化碳和甲烷浓度的上升上，还体现在漂浮的工业副产品云团中。

sentences.en: Sometimes there are radiation leaks.
sentences.zh: 有时会有辐射泄漏。

sentences.en: And all the while, billions of gadgets and antennas cast off a buzzing, planetary swarm of electromagnetic transmissions.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，数十亿的小工具和天线散发出嗡嗡作响的行星级电磁传输群。

sentences.en: Would other planet civilizations be like ours?
sentences.zh: 其他行星文明会像我们一样吗？

sentences.en: Would they create the same telltale chemical and electromagnetic signs, what scientists have recently begun calling technosignatures, that Galileo detected?
sentences.zh: 他们会创造出科学家最近开始称之为“技术签名”的、伽利略号所探测到的那种标志性化学和电磁信号吗？

sentences.en: The search for intelligence beyond Earth has long been defined by an assumption that extraterrestrials would have developed radio technologies akin to what humans have created.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，寻找地球以外的智慧生命一直基于一种假设，即外星人会发展出类似于人类创造的无线电技术。

sentences.en: In some early academic papers on the topic, dating to the late 1950s, scientists even posited that these extraterrestrials might be interested in chatting with us.
sentences.zh: 在一些追溯到 20 世纪 50 年代后期的早期学术论文中，科学家甚至推测这些外星人可能有兴趣与我们聊天。

sentences.en: That played into this whole idea of aliens as salvation.
sentences.zh: 这迎合了将外星人视为救世主的整个想法。

sentences.en: You know, aliens were going to teach us things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，外星人会教我们一些东西。

sentences.en: Adam Frank, an astrophysicist at the University of Rochester, told me recently.
sentences.zh: 罗切斯特大学的天体物理学家亚当·弗兰克最近告诉我。

sentences.en: Frank points out that the search for signals from deep space has, over time, become more agnostic.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克指出，随着时间的推移，寻找深空信号的搜索变得更加不可知论。

sentences.en: Rather than looking for direct calls to Earth, telescopes now sweep the sky, searching billions of frequencies simultaneously for electronic signals whose origins
sentences.zh: 望远镜不再寻找直接呼叫地球的信号，而是同时扫描天空中的数十亿个频率，寻找起源

sentences.en: can't be explained by celestial phenomena.
sentences.zh: 无法用天体现象解释的电子信号。

sentences.en: At the same time, the search for intelligent life has turned in a novel direction.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，寻找智慧生命的搜索转向了一个新的方向。

sentences.en: In 2018, Frank attended a meeting in Houston whose focus was technosignatures.
sentences.zh: 2018 年，弗兰克参加了在休斯敦举行的一次会议，重点是技术签名。

sentences.en: The goal was to get the 60 researchers in attendance to think about defining a new scientific field that,
sentences.zh: 目标是让与会的 60 名研究人员思考如何定义一个新的科学领域，

sentences.en: with NASA's help, would seek out signs of technology on distant worlds, like atmospheric pollution, exploration, to take just one example.
sentences.zh: 在 NASA 的帮助下，寻找遥远世界上的技术迹象，例如大气污染、探索，仅举一例。

sentences.en: That meeting in Houston was the dawn of the new era, at least as I saw it, Frank recalls.
sentences.zh: “休斯敦的那次会议是新时代的黎明，至少在我看来是这样，”弗兰克回忆道。

sentences.en: NASA has a long history of staying out of the extraterrestrial business.
sentences.zh: NASA 在远离外星人事务方面有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: Everybody was sort of there with wide eyes, like, oh my god, is this really happening?
sentences.zh: 每个人都瞪大了眼睛，好像在说，天哪，这真的在发生吗？

sentences.en: The result, at least for Frank, has been a new direction for his work, as well as some money to fund it.
sentences.zh: 对弗兰克而言，结果是他工作的新方向，以及一些资助它的资金。

sentences.en: He and a few astronomy colleagues around the country formed the group Categorizing Atmospheric
sentences.zh: 他和全国各地的几位天文学同事组成了“大气分类”小组

sentences.en: Technosignatures, or CATS, which NASA has since awarded nearly $1 million in grants.
sentences.zh: 技术签名，简称 CATS，NASA 此后授予了该小组近 100 万美元的资助。

sentences.en: The ambition for CATS is to create a library of possible technosignatures.
sentences.zh: CATS 的目标是建立一个可能的技术签名库。

sentences.en: In short, Frank and his colleagues are researching what could constitute evidence that technological civilization exists on other planets.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，弗兰克和他的同事们正在研究什么可以构成其他行星上存在技术文明的证据。

sentences.en: At this stage, Frank stresses, his team's work is not about communicating with aliens, nor is it meant to contribute to research on extraterrestrial radio transmissions.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克强调，在现阶段，他团队的工作不是为了与外星人交流，也不旨在为外星无线电传输的研究做出贡献。

sentences.en: They are instead thinking mainly about the atmospheres of distant worlds, and what those might tell us.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们主要思考遥远世界的大气层，以及这些大气层可能告诉我们什么。

sentences.en: The civilization will just be doing whatever it's doing, and we're making no assumptions about whether anybody wants to communicate or doesn't want to communicate, he says.
sentences.zh: “文明只会做它正在做的事情，我们不对任何人是否想交流或不想交流做任何假设，”他说。

sentences.en: This line of inquiry might not have been productive just a few years ago, but several advances have made the search for technosignatures feasible.
sentences.zh: 这种探究方向在几年前可能还不会有成果，但几项进展使寻找技术签名变得可行。

sentences.en: The first, thanks to new telescopes and astronomical techniques, is the identification of planets orbiting distant stars.
sentences.zh: 首先，得益于新的望远镜和天文技术，我们能够识别围绕遥远恒星运行的行星。

sentences.en: As of August, NASA's confirmed tally of such exoplanets was 5,084, and the number tends to grow by several hundred a year.
sentences.zh: 截至 8 月，NASA 确认的此类系外行星数量为 5084 颗，而且这个数字每年往往会增加几百颗。

sentences.en: Pretty much every star you see in the night sky has a planet around it, if not a family of planets,
sentences.zh: “你夜空中看到的几乎每一颗恒星周围都有行星，如果不是行星家族的话，”

sentences.en: Frank says.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说。

sentences.en: He notes that this realization has only taken hold in the past decade or so.
sentences.zh: 他指出，这种认识在过去十年左右才真正确立。

sentences.en: Because there are probably at least 100 billion stars in the Milky Way galaxy, and an estimated 100
sentences.zh: 因为银河系中可能至少有 1000 亿颗恒星，而宇宙中估计有 1000

sentences.en: billion galaxies in the universe, the potential candidates for life, as well as for civilizations that possess technology, may involve numbers almost too large to imagine.
sentences.zh: 亿个星系，生命的潜在候选者，以及拥有技术的文明，其数量可能大到难以想象。

sentences.en: Perhaps more important, our tools keep getting better.
sentences.zh: 也许更重要的是，我们的工具在不断改进。

sentences.en: This summer, the first pictures from the new James Webb Space Telescope were released.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，新的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜拍摄的第一批照片发布了。

sentences.en: But several other powerful ground- and space-based instruments are being developed that will allow
sentences.zh: 但其他几种强大的地面和空间仪器正在开发中，这将使

sentences.en: us to view exceedingly distant objects for the first time, or view previously identified objects in novel ways.
sentences.zh: 我们能够首次观测到极其遥远的天体，或以新颖的方式观测先前识别的天体。

sentences.en: With things like JWST and some of the other telescopes, we're beginning to be able to
sentences.zh: “有了 JWST 和其他一些望远镜，我们开始能够

sentences.en: probe atmospheres looking for much smaller signals, Michael New, a NASA research official who attended the
sentences.zh: 探测大气层以寻找更微弱的信号，”参加了

sentences.en: 2018 Houston Conference told me.
sentences.zh: 2018 年休斯敦会议的 NASA 研究官员迈克尔·纽告诉我。

sentences.en: And this is something we just couldn't have done before.
sentences.zh: 这是我们以前根本无法做到的事情。

sentences.en: As Frank puts it more bluntly, the point is, after 2500 years of people yelling at each other over life in the universe,
sentences.zh: 正如弗兰克更直白地说的那样，重点是，在人们为宇宙中的生命争论了 2500 年之后，

sentences.en: in the next 10, 20, and 30 years, we will actually get data.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的 10 年、20 年和 30 年里，我们将真正获得数据。

sentences.en: In July, when NASA released the first batch of images from the Webb telescope, we could glimpse remote corners of the universe with newfound clarity and beauty.
sentences.zh: 7 月，当 NASA 发布韦伯望远镜的第一批图像时，我们得以以全新的清晰度和美感一窥宇宙的遥远角落。

sentences.en: A panorama of cosmic cliffs, 24 trillion miles tall, constructed from gas and dust, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如，由气体和尘埃构成的 24 万亿英里高的宇宙悬崖全景。

sentences.en: The images were stunning, but also bewildering.
sentences.zh: 这些图像令人惊叹，但也令人困惑。

sentences.en: They defied description.
sentences.zh: 它们无法用语言描述。

sentences.en: What could we even compare them to?
sentences.zh: 我们甚至能拿什么来比较它们呢？

sentences.en: Webb was reaching farther in distance and into the past than any telescope before it, collecting light from stars
sentences.zh: 韦伯望远镜比以往任何望远镜都更深入地探测距离和过去，收集来自恒星的光，

sentences.en: that in some cases required more than 13 billion years to reach us.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这些光需要超过 130 亿年才能到达我们这里。

sentences.en: We will need to acclimate ourselves to the task of constantly looking at, and interpreting, things we've never seen before.
sentences.zh: 我们需要适应不断观察和解读我们从未见过的事物的任务。

sentences.en: The Webb telescope can look near as well as far.
sentences.zh: 韦伯望远镜既能看近，也能看远。

sentences.en: During its first year, about 7% of its time will be spent observing our own solar system, according to Heidi B.
sentences.zh: 据海蒂·B·哈米尔称，在第一年，它约 7% 的时间将用于观测我们自己的太阳系，

sentences.en: Hamill, an interdisciplinary scientist who worked on the telescope's development.
sentences.zh: 她是一位参与了该望远镜开发的跨学科科学家。

sentences.en: Webb can analyze the atmospheres of nearby planets like Jupiter and Mars using its infrared sensors.
sentences.zh: 韦伯可以使用其红外传感器分析木星和火星等附近行星的大气层。

sentences.en: These capabilities can also be directed at some of the closest Earth-sized exoplanets, like those surrounding the small Trappist-1 star, 40 light years away.
sentences.zh: 这些能力也可以指向一些最近的类地系外行星，比如围绕 40 光年外的小型 Trappist-1 恒星运行的行星。

sentences.en: One goal of that focus is to discern a biosignature, that is, an indication that life exists, or has existed, on those worlds.
sentences.zh: 这一重点的一个目标是辨别生物签名，即表明生命存在于或曾经存在于这些世界上的迹象。

sentences.en: On Earth, a biosignature might be the discarded shell of a clam, the fallen feather of a bird, a fossilized fern embedded in sedimentary rock.
sentences.zh: 在地球上，生物签名可能是蛤蜊丢弃的壳、鸟儿掉落的羽毛、嵌入沉积岩中的化石蕨类植物。

sentences.en: On an exoplanet, it might be a certain ratio of gases, oxygen, methane, H2O, and CO2, say, that suggest the presence of microbes or plants.
sentences.zh: 在系外行星上，它可能是某种气体比例，比如氧气、甲烷、水和二氧化碳，暗示着微生物或植物的存在。

sentences.en: Nicole Lewis, an associate professor of astronomy at
sentences.zh: 康奈尔大学天文学副教授妮可·刘易斯，

sentences.en: Cornell University, whose team has been approved for 22.5 hours of Webb observation time this year to look at
sentences.zh: 她的团队今年已获准使用 22.5 小时的韦伯观测时间来观察

sentences.en: TRAPPIST-1e, one of seven planets circling the TRAPPIST-1 star, told me that well before declaring
sentences.zh: TRAPPIST-1e，即围绕 TRAPPIST-1 恒星运行的七颗行星之一。她告诉我，在宣布

sentences.en: the discovery of a biosignature, she would have to carefully determine the planet's atmosphere and potential habitability.
sentences.zh: 发现生物签名之前，她必须仔细确定行星的大气层和潜在的宜居性。

sentences.en: First, we have to find out if there's air, she says, and then we can ask, what's in the air?
sentences.zh: “首先，我们必须弄清楚是否有空气，”她说，“然后我们才能问，空气里有什么？”

sentences.en: She estimates that it would take three or more years of observing a system to be able to say there's a biosignature.
sentences.zh: 她估计，需要对一个系统进行三年或更长时间的观测，才能说存在生物签名。

sentences.en: Biosignatures and technosignatures point the same way, toward life.
sentences.zh: 生物签名和技术签名指向同一个方向，即生命。

sentences.en: But for now, they are being pursued by two separate scientific communities.
sentences.zh: 但目前，它们正由两个独立的科学界进行研究。

sentences.en: One reason is historical.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是历史性的。

sentences.en: The study of biosignatures, which began in the 1960s within the new discipline of exobiology, has been receiving support from NASA and academic institutions for decades.
sentences.zh: 生物签名的研究始于 20 世纪 60 年代的新兴学科外星生物学，几十年来一直得到 NASA 和学术机构的支持。

sentences.en: But technosignature was coined only recently, in 2007, by Jill Tartar, a pioneering figure in astronomy who has spent her career conducting searches for alien transmissions.
sentences.zh: 但“技术签名”一词直到最近才由吉尔·塔特在 2007 年提出，她是一位天文学先驱，职业生涯一直致力于寻找外星传输信号。

sentences.en: Jason Wright, a professor of astronomy and astrophysics at Penn State who was a member of Frank's
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学的天文学与天体物理学教授杰森·赖特（Jason Wright）曾是弗兰克（Frank）团队的一员，

sentences.en: Katz Group, says he thinks of Tartar's idea as a rebranding of the search for extraterrestrial intelligence, which has long been relegated to the scientific fringe.
sentences.zh: 他表示，他将塔塔尔（Tartar）的观点视为对“搜寻地外文明”这一长期被边缘化的科学领域的一次品牌重塑。

sentences.en: When Jill coined the phrase,
sentences.zh: 赖特告诉我，当吉尔（Jill）提出这个概念时，

sentences.en: Wright told me, she was trying to emphasize that NASA was looking for microbes and slime and atmospheric biosignatures, but technosignatures were really under the same umbrella.
sentences.zh: 她是想强调，虽然美国国家航空航天局（NASA）一直在寻找微生物、黏液和大气生物特征，但“科技特征”其实也属于同一范畴。

sentences.en: Any search for biosignatures on a distant planet, Wright contends, would logically overlap the search for technosignatures, once it became time to explain unusual observations.
sentences.zh: 赖特认为，一旦需要解释某些异常观测结果，任何对遥远行星生物特征的搜寻，在逻辑上都会与科技特征的搜寻产生重叠。

sentences.en: Does a telescopic reading suggest a life-sustaining atmosphere?
sentences.zh: 望远镜的读数是否暗示了存在维持生命的某种大气？

sentences.en: Or is it possibly a sign of technology, too?
sentences.zh: 或者，它是否也可能是某种科技的迹象？

sentences.en: Scientists looking for biosignatures, in other words, may encounter marks of technology as well.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，寻找生物特征的科学家们也可能会偶然发现科技留下的痕迹。

sentences.en: Wright, Frank, and the rest of the Katz team are thus interested in atmospheric markers that would probably never occur naturally.
sentences.zh: 因此，赖特、弗兰克以及凯茨（Katz）团队的其他成员，对那些在自然界中几乎不可能出现的各种大气标记很感兴趣。

sentences.en: One recent group paper, for example, written primarily by Jacob Huck
sentences.zh: 例如，最近该团队发表的一篇论文，主要由雅各布·哈克·米斯拉（Jacob Huck Misra）撰写，

sentences.en: Misra, a Katz member who works at the non-profit Blue Marble Space Institute of Science,
sentences.zh: 他是凯茨团队的一员，在非营利组织“蓝大理石空间科学研究所”（Blue Marble Space Institute of Science）工作，

sentences.en: considers how the presence of chlorofluorocarbons, an industrial byproduct, would give a distinct spectral signal and could be picked up by Webb.
sentences.zh: 该论文探讨了作为工业副产品的氯氟烃（CFCs）如何产生独特的光谱信号，并可能被韦伯望远镜捕捉到。

sentences.en: Huck Misra was also the first author on a recent paper suggesting that an exoplanet with agriculture, exopharms, might emit telltale atmospheric emissions.
sentences.zh: 哈克·米斯拉还是近期另一篇论文的第一作者，该论文提出，拥有农业或“外星农场”的系外行星可能会排放出明显的特征性大气气体。

sentences.en: Another paper, one written mainly by Ravi Koparapu, a Katz member who works at NASA's Goddard Space Flight
sentences.zh: 另一篇主要由拉维·科帕拉普（Ravi Koparapu）撰写的论文——他也是凯茨团队成员，在NASA戈达德太空飞行中心工作——

sentences.en: Center, makes the case that the emission of nitrogen dioxide, an industrial byproduct, could signal the existence of alien technology.
sentences.zh: 论证了作为工业副产品的二氧化氮排放，可能预示着外星科技的存在。

sentences.en: Those emissions might be observable by a NASA space telescope known as LUVOIR, Large Ultraviolet Optical Infrared Surveyor, that is slated to be deployed after 2040.
sentences.zh: 这些排放物或许能被NASA计划在2040年后部署的“大型紫外/光学/红外测量仪”（LUVOIR）太空望远镜观测到。

sentences.en: These scenarios, aliens running factories, say, or aliens riding tractors at harvest time,
sentences.zh: 这些场景——比如外星人经营工厂，或者在收获季节驾驶拖拉机——

sentences.en: might seem unlikely, but the scientists working on technosignatures are comfortable with the low odds.
sentences.zh: 看起来似乎不太可能，但研究科技特征的科学家们并不介意这些微小的概率。

sentences.en: If we focus on what's detectable, based on these instruments that we're building, that's really the fundamental question, Huck Misra told me.
sentences.zh: 哈克·米斯拉告诉我：“如果我们专注于基于我们正在建造的这些仪器所能探测到的东西，那才是最根本的问题。”

sentences.en: When I visited Wright at his office at Penn State in the spring, he made the case that technosignatures are not only more detectable than biosignatures,
sentences.zh: 春天，当我在宾夕法尼亚州立大学的办公室拜访赖特时，他提出，科技特征不仅可能比生物特征更容易被探测到，

sentences.en: possibly, but also more abundant and longer lived.
sentences.zh: 而且可能更丰富、存在的时间也更长。

sentences.en: Consider Earth as an example, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，以地球为例。

sentences.en: Its technology already extends all over the solar system.
sentences.zh: 我们的科技已经延伸到了整个太阳系。

sentences.en: We have junk on the moon.
sentences.zh: 月球上有我们留下的垃圾。

sentences.en: We have rovers driving around Mars.
sentences.zh: 火星上有我们正在行驶的漫游车。

sentences.en: We have satellites orbiting other planets.
sentences.zh: 其他行星轨道上有我们发射的卫星。

sentences.en: What's more, several spacecraft, including two Pioneers, two Voyagers, and the Pluto probe New Horizons, all launched by NASA,
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，NASA发射的几艘航天器，包括两艘先驱者号、两艘旅行者号以及冥王星探测器新视野号，

sentences.en: are venturing beyond the edge of the solar system into interstellar space.
sentences.zh: 都已经冒险飞出了太阳系边缘，进入了星际空间。

sentences.en: Such technosignatures could last billions of years, and we're only 65 years into the age of space exploration.
sentences.zh: 这样的科技特征可以存在数十亿年，而我们进入太空探索时代才不过65年。

sentences.en: An older civilization could have seeded the galaxy with thousands of technosignatures, which could make them easier to detect.
sentences.zh: 一个更古老的文明可能已经在银河系中播撒了数以千计的科技特征，这可能会使它们更容易被发现。

sentences.en: Look, I'm truly agnostic about whether there's even anything to find, Wright said.
sentences.zh: “听着，对于到底有没有东西可以发现，我持真正的不可知论态度，”赖特说。

sentences.en: In 1961, he pointed out, the astronomer Frank Drake presented what's now known as the Drake Equation, which is made up of many variables and attempts to help
sentences.zh: 他指出，1961年，天文学家弗兰克·德雷克（Frank Drake）提出了现在广为人知的“德雷克方程”，该方程由许多变量组成，旨在帮助

sentences.en: calculate the number of intelligent civilizations elsewhere in the galaxy.
sentences.zh: 计算银河系中其他地方智慧文明的数量。

sentences.en: But with so little data to plug into the variables, there has yet to be any solution to the equation.
sentences.zh: 但由于代入变量的数据太少，这个方程至今还没有任何解。

sentences.en: For Wright, Drake's equation at least allows for a plausibility that something is out there.
sentences.zh: 对赖特来说，德雷克方程至少提供了一种“外星存在”的可能性。

sentences.en: But is it life or complex life?
sentences.zh: 但那是生命，还是复杂的生命？

sentences.en: Bio-signatures, Wright said, are going to be extremely challenging to detect, if they exiSt. So that's two big ifs.
sentences.zh: 赖特说，如果生物特征真的存在，探测它们的难度将极大。所以，这里有两个巨大的“如果”。

sentences.en: It's very possible that life is just so rare that there's nothing within a kiloparsec for us to find.
sentences.zh: 生命极其罕见，以至于在我们一千秒差距（kiloparsec）的范围内可能什么都没有，这种情况是非常可能的。

sentences.en: But technology, he explained, could have started the same distance away.
sentences.zh: 但他解释说，科技可能在同样的距离外就已经开始了。

sentences.en: A kiloparsec is 3,261 light-years in distance, and moved closer to Earth over eons.
sentences.zh: 一千秒差距相当于3261光年的距离，并且随着时间的推移，它可能已经向地球靠近了。

sentences.en: It could be a traveling probe, like one of our voyagers, or a systematic species migration.
sentences.zh: 它可能是一个像我们旅行者号那样的飞行探测器，也可能是一个系统性的物种迁移。

sentences.en: It could be an electronic signal sent
sentences.zh: 它可能是一个在3250年前发送的电子信号，

sentences.en: 3,250 years ago, and moving at the speed of light, just coming into our range.
sentences.zh: 以光速传播，现在刚刚进入我们的探测范围。

sentences.en: So we have a much bigger search radius for technology, Wright said.
sentences.zh: “所以，我们搜寻科技的半径要大得多，”赖特说。

sentences.en: But also, perhaps complex life that builds technology is itself extremely rare, even when life forMs. He paused.
sentences.zh: “但同样，也许即使生命形成了，能够创造科技的复杂生命本身也极其罕见。”他停顿了一下。

sentences.en: I don't know, he said.
sentences.zh: “我不知道，”他说。

sentences.en: What drives me is not the idea that we will find something in my lifetime.
sentences.zh: “驱动我的不是那种‘我这辈子能发现什么’的想法。”

sentences.en: What drives me is that we're not looking very well.
sentences.zh: “驱动我的是，我们目前的搜寻工作做得还不够好。”

sentences.en: And it's too important a search, answering too important a question, not to do well.
sentences.zh: “这是一项太重要的搜寻，回答的是一个太重要的问题，我们不能做得不好。”

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: The giggle factor.
sentences.zh: “咯咯笑因素”（Giggle factor）。

sentences.en: That's what anyone who does research on extraterrestrials is bound to encounter, according to Frank.
sentences.zh: 据弗兰克说，任何研究地外文明的人都注定会遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: As a graduate student in the 80s, Frank was wary of the field as a career move.
sentences.zh: 作为80年代的研究生，弗兰克曾对将此作为职业方向持谨慎态度。

sentences.en: I'd never worked in this before.
sentences.zh: “我以前从未从事过这方面的工作。”

sentences.en: I'd never published any papers, he told me, referring to his pre-technosignature research.
sentences.zh: “我从未发表过任何相关论文，”他告诉我，指的是他研究科技特征之前的经历。

sentences.en: His reluctance was reinforced by the marginalization of the subject.
sentences.zh: 这种学科被边缘化的现状，加剧了他的犹豫。

sentences.en: Early on in the 1970s, NASA had shown a willingness to fund radio telescope searches for extraterrestrial activity.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪70年代，NASA曾表现出资助射电望远镜搜寻地外活动的意愿。

sentences.en: But the search for aliens aroused opposition.
sentences.zh: 但搜寻外星人的行为招致了反对。

sentences.en: In 1978, Senator William Proxmire declared that taxpayers were being fleeced, a criticism
sentences.zh: 1978年，参议员威廉·普罗克斯迈尔（William Proxmire）宣称纳税人的钱被浪费了，这一批评

sentences.en: NASA heeded by striking the search for extraterrestrials from its budget.
sentences.zh: 促使NASA从预算中删除了搜寻地外文明的项目。

sentences.en: The agency was willing to back survey projects again in the 1980s, but another senator, Richard Bryan, stopped the programs in 1993.
sentences.zh: 80年代，该机构曾愿意再次支持调查项目，但另一位参议员理查德·布莱恩（Richard Bryan）在1993年叫停了这些计划。

sentences.en: This hopefully will be the end of Martian hunting at the taxpayers' expense, Bryan said at the time.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩当时说：“希望这将是纳税人资助的‘火星狩猎’的终结。”

sentences.en: Only recently has the stigma begun to wear off.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，这种污名才开始消退。

sentences.en: At the urging of the Texas representative,
sentences.zh: 在时任众议院科学委员会主席、现已退休的德克萨斯州众议员

sentences.en: Lamar Smith, now retired, who was chairman of the House Science Committee, a bill was introduced in Congress for NASA to allocate $10 million to technosignatures.
sentences.zh: 拉马尔·史密斯（Lamar Smith）的敦促下，国会提出了一项法案，要求NASA为科技特征研究拨款1000万美元。

sentences.en: NASA quickly asked for a forum to get a clearer sense of what research was worth funding, positioning the effort as a departure from radio astronomy.
sentences.zh: NASA迅速要求召开论坛，以更清楚地了解哪些研究值得资助，并将此项工作定位为对射电天文学的拓展。

sentences.en: I was told the workshop had to be in a certain Texas congressional district,
sentences.zh: “我被告知研讨会必须在特定的德克萨斯州国会选区举行，”

sentences.en: Wright, who was asked to organize the Houston meeting, told me.
sentences.zh: 被邀请组织休斯顿会议的赖特告诉我。

sentences.en: When Frank, who trained as a theoretical astrophysicist rather than an observational astronomer, attended the Houston
sentences.zh: 当弗兰克——他受训成为的是理论天体物理学家，而非观测天文学家——参加休斯顿

sentences.en: meeting, he had been writing about how civilizations alter their planetary atmospheres.
sentences.zh: 会议时，他一直在撰写关于文明如何改变其行星大气的文章。

sentences.en: Because humans have changed our world so significantly through global warming, essentially by burning wood and fossil fuels, he had been wondering if this would happen everywhere.
sentences.zh: 因为人类通过燃烧木材和化石燃料导致全球变暖，从而显著改变了我们的世界，他一直在思考这是否会在各地发生。

sentences.en: When you pull back and think of the evolution of any planet, you find that what we're going through may be a common transition that you do or don't make it through, Frank says.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说：“当你退后一步思考任何行星的演化时，你会发现我们所经历的可能是一个共同的过渡阶段，无论你是否能挺过去。”

sentences.en: In his view, any species that expands and grows is probably going to create significant feedback effects on its planet.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，任何扩张和发展的物种，都可能会对其行星产生重大的反馈效应。

sentences.en: Civilizations are basically focused on harvesting energy and putting it to work, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，文明基本上专注于获取能源并将其投入使用。

sentences.en: And there should be unintentional markers when you do that.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，应该会留下无意的标记。

sentences.en: You're leaving traces.
sentences.zh: 你正在留下痕迹。

sentences.en: You're creating technosignatures.
sentences.zh: 你正在创造科技特征。

sentences.en: Such assumptions about energy generation and activity are mostly what guide the Katz group.
sentences.zh: 关于能源产生和活动的这些假设，主要是凯茨团队的研究指南。

sentences.en: One day in early May, I sat in on their monthly meeting, which takes place online.
sentences.zh: 五月初的一天，我旁听了他们在线举行的月度会议。

sentences.en: Frank led the discussion from his office in Rochester.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克在他的罗切斯特办公室主持了讨论。

sentences.en: Wright joined from Penn State, Huck Misra from Delaware, Koparapu from Maryland.
sentences.zh: 赖特从宾夕法尼亚州立大学加入，哈克·米斯拉从特拉华州加入，科帕拉普从马里兰州加入。

sentences.en: Another team member,
sentences.zh: 另一位团队成员，

sentences.en: Sophia Shaikh, joined from San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚·谢赫（Sophia Shaikh），从旧金山加入。

sentences.en: A few other contributors tuned in, too.
sentences.zh: 还有几位其他贡献者也参与了会议。

sentences.en: The first order of business was planning for a four-day technosignatures conference at Penn State, organized by Wright for late June, just weeks away.
sentences.zh: 首要议程是为赖特组织的、将于几周后（6月底）在宾夕法尼亚州立大学举行的为期四天的科技特征会议做规划。

sentences.en: This is the first time we'll all be together, physically, since the 2018 meeting in Houston,
sentences.zh: “这是自2018年休斯顿会议以来，我们所有人第一次聚在一起，”

sentences.en: Frank said enthusiastically.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克热情地说。

sentences.en: I think we want to advertise how much progress has happened.
sentences.zh: “我想我们应该宣传一下我们取得了多大的进展。”

sentences.en: He quickly mentioned the chlorofluorocarbons work, the exopharm paper, and the visibility of nitrogen pollutants from afar.
sentences.zh: 他迅速提到了氯氟烃的研究、外星农场论文，以及从远处观察氮污染物的可能性。

sentences.en: When Koparapu's turn came, he explained the relationship of the team's ideas to the specifications of current and future telescopes.
sentences.zh: 轮到科帕拉普时，他解释了团队的构想与当前及未来望远镜规格之间的关系。

sentences.en: Some next-generation projects involve ground-based instruments that are much more powerful and sophisticated than what exists today.
sentences.zh: 一些下一代项目涉及地面仪器，它们比现有的仪器强大且复杂得多。

sentences.en: For instance, the giant Magellan telescope, now under construction in Chile, and the 30-meter telescope planned for
sentences.zh: 例如，目前正在智利建造的巨型麦哲伦望远镜，以及计划在

sentences.en: Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷建造的30米望远镜。

sentences.en: For the Katz group, the most important of these future missions include LUVOIR and HABEX,
sentences.zh: 对于凯茨团队来说，这些未来任务中最重要的是LUVOIR和HABEX，

sentences.en: Habitable Exoplanet Observatory, multi-billion-dollar space telescopes that, unlike Webb, are to be built and calibrated expressly for the study of distant Earth-like planets.
sentences.zh: 即“宜居系外行星天文台”。这些耗资数十亿美元的太空望远镜与韦伯不同，它们是专门为研究遥远的类地行星而建造和校准的。

sentences.en: These devices, only one of which may be built, are two decades away from deployment, however.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些设备（可能只会建造其中一个）距离部署还有二十年。

sentences.en: And for the time being, exoplanet study will largely depend on Webb.
sentences.zh: 目前，系外行星的研究在很大程度上仍将依赖韦伯望远镜。

sentences.en: Once a year, a call goes out for proposals from researchers who want to use the telescope.
sentences.zh: 每年，研究人员都会收到一份提案征集通知，希望使用该望远镜。

sentences.en: Fainter objects in the sky generally require more time, brighter objects less.
sentences.zh: 天空中的暗淡目标通常需要更多时间，明亮目标则较少。

sentences.en: The competition for a slot is fierce, Eric Smith, Webb's program scientist, told me.
sentences.zh: 韦伯的项目科学家埃里克·史密斯（Eric Smith）告诉我，争夺观测时间的竞争非常激烈。

sentences.en: Because so many requests are rejected, last year the telescope reviewed about 1,200 proposals and awarded time to 286 winners, the proposals have to be compelling.
sentences.zh: 由于太多的申请被拒绝——去年望远镜审核了约1200份提案，仅授予了286名获胜者观测时间——提案必须非常有说服力。

sentences.en: According to Smith, the competition is likely to become even greater in the coming years, now that the scientific community has seen what the telescope can do.
sentences.zh: 据史密斯称，随着科学界已经见识到了该望远镜的能力，未来几年的竞争可能会更加激烈。

sentences.en: Frank told me that he believes that his team, or other scientists taking a cue from
sentences.zh: 弗兰克告诉我，他相信他的团队，或者其他受到

sentences.en: his team's techno-signature research, are probably a few years away from making a formal requeSt.
sentences.zh: 他团队科技特征研究启发的科学家们，可能再过几年就能提出正式申请了。

sentences.en: If we're going to ask for 100 hours of James Webb time, we better have every possibility worked out, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“如果我们打算申请100小时的詹姆斯·韦伯观测时间，我们最好把每一种可能性都考虑周全。”

sentences.en: They're not going to give us that unless we've shown that this is exactly where to look, this is the signal-to-noise ratio we expect, and so on.
sentences.zh: “除非我们证明了这就是该看的地方，这就是我们预期的信噪比等等，否则他们是不会给我们的。”

sentences.en: In the CATS meeting, the brainstorming covered a mix of old and new ideas.
sentences.zh: 在凯茨团队的会议上，头脑风暴涵盖了新旧想法的结合。

sentences.en: The techno-signatures field is open to looking for inspiration anywhere, even in concepts that
sentences.zh: 科技特征领域对从任何地方寻找灵感持开放态度，即使是那些

sentences.en: might have appeared decades earlier in journals or in obscure conference proceedings before being dismissed or forgotten.
sentences.zh: 几十年前可能出现在期刊或晦涩的会议记录中，随后被驳回或遗忘的概念。

sentences.en: A 1961 paper on interstellar laser communication, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，一篇关于星际激光通信的1961年论文。

sentences.en: At this meeting, there was talk of service worlds, where a civilization develops a nearby planet or moon, not for habitation, but for, say, energy harvesting.
sentences.zh: 在这次会议上，有人谈到了“服务世界”（service worlds），即一个文明开发附近的行星或卫星，不是为了居住，而是为了，比如，能源采集。

sentences.en: It is an idea sometimes that sometimes contemplated in science fiction.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有时在科幻小说中被构思的想法。

sentences.en: But in this instance, the notion first arose from a paper that a member of the CATS group co-wrote a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，这个概念最初源于凯茨团队的一名成员几年前合写的一篇论文。

sentences.en: On a service world, terrain might be covered entirely with photovoltaic panels that reflect part of the light spectrum back into space,
sentences.zh: 在一个服务世界上，地形可能完全被光伏电池板覆盖，将部分光谱反射回太空，

sentences.en: a reflection that could be discernible trillions of miles away.
sentences.zh: 这种反射在数万亿英里外可能是可以辨认的。

sentences.en: A service world wouldn't even have a bio-signature, Frank said.
sentences.zh: “服务世界甚至不会有生物特征，”弗兰克说。

sentences.en: It's just a pure techno-signature.
sentences.zh: “它纯粹就是一个科技特征。”

sentences.en: Sheik then mentioned something she had been thinking about lately, microplastic pollution in oceans, now an Earth techno-signature.
sentences.zh: 谢赫随后提到了她最近一直在思考的事情：海洋中的微塑料污染，现在已成为地球的一种科技特征。

sentences.en: You can see it if you scoop up a glass of water and look at it under a microscope.
sentences.zh: 如果你舀起一杯水并在显微镜下观察，就能看到它。

sentences.en: It's very obvious in situ, she said.
sentences.zh: “在现场观察非常明显，”她说。

sentences.en: But is there any way to detect that remotely?
sentences.zh: “但有没有办法远程探测到它呢？”

sentences.en: So I just decided to check.
sentences.zh: “所以我决定查一下。”

sentences.en: It seemed kind of silly.
sentences.zh: “这看起来有点傻。”

sentences.en: While reading academic papers, she told the group, she found that scientists are trying to spot plastic in our oceans using radar satellites.
sentences.zh: 她告诉团队，在阅读学术论文时，她发现科学家们正试图利用雷达卫星来发现我们海洋中的塑料。

sentences.en: So they're using remote sensing to look for changes in viscosity of ocean water, which is indicative of microplastics.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在使用遥感技术来寻找海水粘度的变化，这正是微塑料存在的迹象。

sentences.en: And it seems like it actually works.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来它确实有效。

sentences.en: As the discussion wound down, Frank raised something else.
sentences.zh: 随着讨论接近尾声，弗兰克提出了另一件事。

sentences.en: Oxygen and combustion as a techno-signature.
sentences.zh: 氧气和燃烧作为一种科技特征。

sentences.en: This in turn raised an issue about ocean worlds.
sentences.zh: 这反过来引发了一个关于海洋世界的问题。

sentences.en: Could they, he asked, produce species that develop technology?
sentences.zh: 他问道，它们能产生发展出科技的物种吗？

sentences.en: If you can't start a fire underwater, how does an ocean-going species learn to do metallurgy?
sentences.zh: 如果你不能在水下生火，海洋物种如何学会冶金？

sentences.en: The question was not a whimsy.
sentences.zh: 这个问题并非异想天开。

sentences.en: Many exoplanets are thought to be complete water worlds.
sentences.zh: 许多系外行星被认为是完全的海洋世界。

sentences.en: Earth, about one-third of which is land, might be an exception.
sentences.zh: 地球约三分之一是陆地，这可能是一个例外。

sentences.en: The group debated where an ocean species could find energy.
sentences.zh: 团队讨论了海洋物种可以在哪里找到能源。

sentences.en: Hydrothermal vents, Huck Misra offered.
sentences.zh: 哈克·米斯拉提议：“热液喷口。”

sentences.en: Others suggested chemical reactions that produce heat without combustion.
sentences.zh: 其他人建议使用无需燃烧即可产生热量的化学反应。

sentences.en: Frank said he still wondered if fire in an oxygen-rich environment is a prerequisite to development.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说他仍然想知道，在富氧环境中生火是否是发展的先决条件。

sentences.en: That's why we're thinking about combustion, he said.
sentences.zh: “这就是为什么我们在考虑燃烧，”他说。

sentences.en: You're not going to start with nuclear power, right?
sentences.zh: “你不可能从核能开始，对吧？”

sentences.en: It just seems very anthropocentric, Nick Toussaint, a Penn State graduate student on the call, said.
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学的研究生尼克·图桑（Nick Toussaint）在通话中说：“这看起来非常以人类为中心。”

sentences.en: Just because that's the way we did it, does it mean everyone else would?
sentences.zh: “仅仅因为那是我们的做法，就意味着其他人也会这样做吗？”

sentences.en: What if you have a civilization of octopuses?
sentences.zh: “如果你有一个章鱼文明呢？”

sentences.en: The comment prompted Shaikh to share some links to academic studies.
sentences.zh: 这条评论促使 Shaikh 分享了一些学术研究的链接。

sentences.en: There's actually this cool literature about tool development and aquatic animals, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，实际上有一些关于工具开发和水生动物的很酷的文献。

sentences.en: Underwater tool development has been hard to observe, as she understood it, but it's real, and it could mean that combustion is not the only route to sophistication.
sentences.zh: 据她理解，水下工具的开发一直很难观察到，但它是真实存在的，这可能意味着燃烧并不是通往文明的唯一途径。

sentences.en: A number of species also use water pressure or bubbles, or other species, as tools.
sentences.zh: 许多物种也利用水压、气泡或其他物种作为工具。

sentences.en: I think there's a lot to explore there, she added.
sentences.zh: 她补充说，我认为那里有很多值得探索的地方。

sentences.en: Frank seemed inclined to put off the discussion until next time.
sentences.zh: Frank 似乎倾向于把讨论推迟到下次进行。

sentences.en: Still, as the meeting ended, the comments demonstrated how challenging it can be for the team to conceptualize other worlds.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，会议结束时，这些评论表明，对于团队来说，构想其他世界是多么具有挑战性。

sentences.en: Their conversation likewise suggested that we know far less than we might think about our own.
sentences.zh: 他们的谈话同样表明，我们对自己世界的了解远比我们想象的要少。

sentences.en: To imagine the unimaginable, Ravi Koparapu told me one day, we must reorient our minds.
sentences.zh: Ravi Koparapu 有一天告诉我，为了想象不可想象的事物，我们必须重新调整我们的思维。

sentences.en: The problem is that the technosignatures field relies, for now, on a small data set, a single planet, Earth, where we know a species has arisen that
sentences.zh: 问题在于，技术签名领域目前依赖于一个很小的数据集，即我们所知的唯一一颗行星——地球，在这里我们知道出现了一个物种，它

sentences.en: created gadgetry, made pollution, and altered its atmosphere, dangerously so.
sentences.zh: 制造了装置，造成了污染，并改变了大气层，而且是危险的改变。

sentences.en: The CATS members, Koparapu says, understand this as a liability, but also as a requisite first step.
sentences.zh: Koparapu 说，CATS 的成员们明白这既是一种负担，也是必要的第一步。

sentences.en: If you go to a party where you know hardly anyone, Koparapu says, the first thing you do is go to someone that you recognize so you can start up the conversation.
sentences.zh: Koparapu 说，如果你去参加一个几乎不认识任何人的聚会，你做的第一件事就是去找一个你认识的人，这样你就可以开始交谈了。

sentences.en: During my visit to Frank, he told me that as difficult as it is for humans to imagine alien species, imagining long time frames is equally challenging.
sentences.zh: 在我拜访 Frank 期间，他告诉我，人类想象外星物种很困难，而想象漫长的时间跨度同样具有挑战性。

sentences.en: Modern science as a discipline is only about 500 years old.
sentences.zh: 现代科学作为一门学科只有大约 500 年的历史。

sentences.en: The transistor, the building block of modern technologies, is around 75 years old.
sentences.zh: 晶体管是现代技术的基础，大约有 75 年的历史。

sentences.en: The first iPhone came out
sentences.zh: 第一部 iPhone 发布于

sentences.en: 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 15 年前。

sentences.en: How would a technological society evolve over 10,000 years?
sentences.zh: 一个技术社会在 10,000 年间会如何演变？

sentences.en: Over a million?
sentences.zh: 在一百万年间呢？

sentences.en: Frank notes that there may be many other ways to define a civilization beyond what his group has been focusing on.
sentences.zh: Frank 指出，除了他团队所关注的之外，可能还有许多其他定义文明的方式。

sentences.en: Rather than builders of big antennas, extraterrestrials could be more like trees in a grove, communicating through threads of fungi underground.
sentences.zh: 外星人可能不像建造大型天线的人，而更像是树林里的树木，通过地下的真菌丝进行交流。

sentences.en: Rather than creators of dirty power plants, aliens might be like octopuses, using tools in ice-crusted oceans.
sentences.zh: 外星人可能不像制造肮脏发电厂的创造者，而更像是章鱼，在冰壳覆盖的海洋中使用工具。

sentences.en: Some theorists have even posited that an ancient society could discard matter altogether, choosing to supplant itself with a diaphanous and undying form of artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 一些理论家甚至提出，一个古老的社会可能会完全抛弃物质，选择用一种透明且永恒的人工智能形式来取代自身。

sentences.en: I can imagine biologies that are much different.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象出截然不同的生物学形态。

sentences.en: I can imagine minds that are much different, Frank says.
sentences.zh: Frank 说，我可以想象出截然不同的思维方式。

sentences.en: For civilizations that we can detect through our instruments, though, he is still convinced that the logical approach is to focus on energy and the consequences of its use.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于我们能通过仪器探测到的文明，他仍然坚信，合乎逻辑的方法是关注能源及其使用带来的后果。

sentences.en: He is not inflexible, though.
sentences.zh: 但他并非一成不变。

sentences.en: Since the meeting in
sentences.zh: 自那次在

sentences.en: Houston, Frank told me, some of his old assumptions and biases have been challenged.
sentences.zh: 休斯顿的会议以来，Frank 告诉我，他的一些旧假设和偏见受到了挑战。

sentences.en: This includes the possibility that our familiarity with Western technology can trap us.
sentences.zh: 这包括我们对西方技术的熟悉可能会束缚我们这一可能性。

sentences.en: He and some of the CATS members have been influenced by critiques of the search for extraterrestrials, chronicled in part in a recent issue of the
sentences.zh: 他和一些 CATS 成员受到了对外星探索批评的影响，这些批评部分记录在最近一期的

sentences.en: American Indian Culture and Research Journal, that challenge our tendency to view industry and gadgetry as the primary indicators of advancement.
sentences.zh: 《美洲印第安文化与研究杂志》上，这些批评挑战了我们将工业和装置视为进步的主要指标的倾向。

sentences.en: Frank pointed out that some indigenous cultures regard the whole natural world as intelligent.
sentences.zh: Frank 指出，一些土著文化认为整个自然界都是有智慧的。

sentences.en: He has become wary, too, of grand, deterministic anthropological narratives he once saw as persuasive.
sentences.zh: 他也开始对那些他曾经认为有说服力的宏大、决定论的人类学叙事保持警惕。

sentences.en: The idea that we were egalitarian hunter-gatherers, and then there was the agricultural revolution, and then came villages, which turned into empires, and that then led to
sentences.zh: 那种认为我们曾经是平等主义的狩猎采集者，然后发生了农业革命，接着出现了村庄，演变成了帝国，并最终导致了

sentences.en: capitalism and science.
sentences.zh: 资本主义和科学的观点。

sentences.en: A new book, The Dawn of Everything by David Graeber and David Wengrow, argues that research data from the last 30 years doesn't support a story of such linear advancement.
sentences.zh: 一本名为《万物之始》（The Dawn of Everything）的新书，由 David Graeber 和 David Wengrow 合著，认为过去 30 年的研究数据并不支持这种线性进步的故事。

sentences.en: It has persuaded Frank that different and unpredictable paths for social and political arrangements, and technology, too, are possible anywhere.
sentences.zh: 它说服了 Frank，认为社会和政治安排以及技术在任何地方都可能存在不同且不可预测的路径。

sentences.en: He has begun to seek out historians, anthropologists, sociologists, biologists, and futurists to help his group narrow the possibilities.
sentences.zh: 他已开始寻找历史学家、人类学家、社会学家、生物学家和未来学家，以帮助他的团队缩小可能性范围。

sentences.en: Catherine Denning is an archaeologist at York University in
sentences.zh: Catherine Denning 是约克大学的一名考古学家，位于

sentences.en: Canada and a longtime contrarian voice in the extraterrestrial search community.
sentences.zh: 加拿大，也是外星探索界长期以来的反对派声音。

sentences.en: The social evolutionary story of humans on
sentences.zh: 她最近告诉我，地球上人类的社会进化史

sentences.en: Earth is not a simple unilinear upward trajectory, she told me recently.
sentences.zh: 并不是一条简单的单向向上轨迹。

sentences.en: And we shouldn't think of aliens that way either.
sentences.zh: 我们也不应该那样看待外星人。

sentences.en: Many societies on Earth have fallen apart and rebuilt from their ruins, Denning points out.
sentences.zh: Denning 指出，地球上的许多社会都曾分崩离析，并从废墟中重建。

sentences.en: And many have never sought to become conquerors.
sentences.zh: 而且许多社会从未寻求成为征服者。

sentences.en: And yet public intellectuals have often rendered the future in ways that give their
sentences.zh: 然而，公共知识分子经常以某种方式描绘未来，使他们的

sentences.en: declarations of high-tech destiny, gleaming megacities and roving starships, an air of certainty.
sentences.zh: 高科技命运宣言、闪闪发光的超级城市和漫游的星际飞船，带有一种确定性的气息。

sentences.en: We might ascribe that to cultural hubris.
sentences.zh: 我们或许可以将其归因于文化傲慢。

sentences.en: At the June technosignatures meeting at Penn State, many presentations were given over to the cat's work as well as traditional extraterrestrial research involving radio astronomy.
sentences.zh: 在六月份于宾夕法尼亚州立大学举行的技术签名会议上，许多演讲都致力于 CATS 的工作以及涉及射电天文学的传统外星研究。

sentences.en: But there were also Denning and Hilding Nielsen, an indigenous astronomer and astrophysicist from the Memorial University of Newfoundland.
sentences.zh: 但 Denning 和 Hilding Nielsen 也参加了会议，Nielsen 是一位来自纽芬兰纪念大学的土著天文学家和天体物理学家。

sentences.en: Nielsen challenged the audience to think about how some indigenous societies were at least thousands of years old, older than science itself.
sentences.zh: Nielsen 向听众提出挑战，让他们思考一些土著社会至少有几千年的历史，比科学本身还要古老。

sentences.en: And yet he wondered if they were considered advanced by Western definitions.
sentences.zh: 然而他想知道，按照西方的定义，他们是否被认为是先进的。

sentences.en: In the case of looking for life elsewhere, he remarked, we're really looking for ourselves in space.
sentences.zh: 他评论说，在寻找其他地方的生命时，我们实际上是在太空中寻找我们自己。

sentences.en: The cat's group appears to be able to avoid that trap.
sentences.zh: CATS 团队似乎能够避免那个陷阱。

sentences.en: At the Penn State meeting, not long after Nielsen's talk, I wandered into a lounge and ended up listening to a coffee break debate among Frank, Shake, and Wright.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州立大学的会议上，Nielsen 的演讲结束后不久，我溜进了一个休息室，最终听到了 Frank、Shake 和 Wright 之间的一场茶歇辩论。

sentences.en: They were discussing a lecture by a colleague who proposed to find a technosignature in the glow of sodium lights, commonly used in street lamps.
sentences.zh: 他们正在讨论一位同事的讲座，该同事提议在钠灯（常用于路灯）的光芒中寻找技术签名。

sentences.en: A strong enough signal could be detectable through some telescopes if, say, an exoplanet were completely covered in urban development.
sentences.zh: 如果一颗系外行星完全被城市开发所覆盖，那么足够强的信号可以通过某些望远镜探测到。

sentences.en: But any technosignatures idea must go through the gantlet of group skepticism.
sentences.zh: 但任何技术签名的想法都必须经过团队怀疑论的考验。

sentences.en: Frank and Shake wondered if sodium light would be used by a civilization that developed differently.
sentences.zh: Frank 和 Shake 想知道，一个以不同方式发展的文明是否会使用钠灯。

sentences.en: Perhaps their eyes would function in different parts of the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 也许他们的眼睛会在光谱的不同部分发挥作用。

sentences.en: Or perhaps they would live underground?
sentences.zh: 或者也许他们住在地下？

sentences.en: If you're a creature that can't see, if you're like a bat that used echolocation, would you even need lights?
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个看不见的生物，如果你像使用回声定位的蝙蝠一样，你甚至需要灯光吗？

sentences.en: Frank said.
sentences.zh: Frank 说。

sentences.en: Would you even know you're part of the galaxy and this larger world?
sentences.zh: 你甚至会知道你是银河系和这个更大世界的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Shake asked.
sentences.zh: Shake 问道。

sentences.en: Would you even look up at the stars?
sentences.zh: 你甚至会抬头看星星吗？

sentences.en: Frank added.
sentences.zh: Frank 补充道。

sentences.en: I mean, if you couldn't see, would you even know they're there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看不见，你甚至会知道它们在那里吗？

sentences.en: Frank turned to me.
sentences.zh: Frank 转过身对我说。

sentences.en: That's what's so extraordinary about this, he said, meaning the maze he and the group wander through.
sentences.zh: 这就是这件事最非凡的地方，他说，指的是他和团队正在探索的迷宫。

sentences.en: They have to rethink evolution, technology, culture, and the meaning of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他们必须重新思考进化、技术、文化和智慧的含义。

sentences.en: But you always have to come back to the fact that we're building a telescope, he added.
sentences.zh: 但他补充说，你总是必须回到我们正在建造望远镜这一事实。

sentences.en: What sensors should it have to find a technosignature?
sentences.zh: 它应该具备什么传感器来寻找技术签名？

sentences.en: He laughed, seemingly at the sheer number of details that would someday need to be worked out.
sentences.zh: 他笑了，似乎是因为总有一天需要解决的细节数量之多。

sentences.en: Also, what screws should it use?
sentences.zh: 另外，它应该使用什么螺丝？

sentences.en: Flathead, Phillips head, or hex nut?
sentences.zh: 一字槽、十字槽还是六角螺母？

sentences.en: Officially,
sentences.zh: 官方而言，

sentences.en: NASA considers the work on technosignatures to be high risk, high reward.
sentences.zh: NASA 认为技术签名的研究属于高风险、高回报的项目。

sentences.en: The risk, in dollars, is modest for now.
sentences.zh: 目前，以美元计算的风险是适度的。

sentences.en: The amount allocated by the agency is minuscule in comparison to, say, the $93 billion being invested over the next few years in its Artemis moon mission.
sentences.zh: 与未来几年投入其“阿尔忒弥斯”登月任务的 930 亿美元相比，该机构分配的金额微不足道。

sentences.en: But moving on to a next step, which would mean devoting precious time for technosignatures
sentences.zh: 但迈向下一步，这意味着要为韦伯望远镜上的技术签名研究投入宝贵的时间，

sentences.en: research on a telescope like Webb, or building an entirely new space-based instrument, would involve a sizable investment.
sentences.zh: 或者建造一个全新的天基仪器，这将涉及相当大的投资。

sentences.en: As for rewards, the development of a technosignatures discipline might mirror that of astrobiology, which arose 25 years ago in response to the discovery of exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 至于回报，技术签名学科的发展可能与天体生物学相似，后者在 25 年前因系外行星的发现而兴起。

sentences.en: In contemplating biosignatures, astrobiologists gained new knowledge into how basic life on Earth can endure in extreme environments, under ice caps, for example, or
sentences.zh: 在思考生物签名时，天体生物学家获得了关于地球上的基本生命如何在极端环境中生存的新知识，例如在冰盖下，或者

sentences.en: near hydrothermal vents.
sentences.zh: 在热液喷口附近。

sentences.en: Thinking about far-off things yielded insights close to home.
sentences.zh: 思考遥远的事物产生了对近处事物的洞察。

sentences.en: The ultimate success for the technosignature team would be an instance of someone using a cat's research to identify signs of a technological civilization.
sentences.zh: 技术签名团队的最终成功将是有人利用 CATS 的研究来识别技术文明迹象的案例。

sentences.en: That would be like the dog who is running and catches the car, Koparapu told me.
sentences.zh: Koparapu 告诉我，那就像一只奔跑并追上汽车的狗。

sentences.en: What would we do next?
sentences.zh: 我们接下来会做什么？

sentences.en: He and Frank both think it's possible that we would do nothing.
sentences.zh: 他和 Frank 都认为，我们什么都不做是有可能的。

sentences.en: At least, not right away.
sentences.zh: 至少，不会马上做。

sentences.en: While there exists a growing body of literature about first contact protocols, we might just monitor a distant technosignature for decades, or perhaps
sentences.zh: 虽然关于第一次接触协议的文献越来越多，但我们可能只是监测一个遥远的技术签名几十年，或者也许

sentences.en: centuries, taking readings with increasingly better telescopes.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪，用越来越好的望远镜进行读数。

sentences.en: And then, maybe, we might send a space probe or message.
sentences.zh: 然后，也许，我们可能会发送一个太空探测器或信息。

sentences.en: Because distances are so vast, it's not lost on the researchers that in viewing an apparently bustling exoplanet from, say, 50 light-years away, we would see
sentences.zh: 因为距离太遥远了，研究人员并没有忽略这样一个事实：在观察一颗看似繁忙的系外行星时，比如从 50 光年外观察，我们会看到

sentences.en: the spectra of technology from 50 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 50 年前的技术光谱。

sentences.en: To send an electronic message and receive a response would, and best, take 100 years.
sentences.zh: 发送一条电子信息并收到回复，充其量需要 100 年。

sentences.en: An actual journey could take millenniuMs.
sentences.zh: 实际的旅程可能需要几千年。

sentences.en: But the work may turn out to have utility beyond the contact scenario or headline-grabbing discovery.
sentences.zh: 但这项工作最终可能会在接触场景或引人注目的发现之外具有实用价值。

sentences.en: Since the 1950s, one of the defining ideas in the search for extraterrestrials has been the
sentences.zh: 自 20 世纪 50 年代以来，外星探索中决定性的思想之一就是

sentences.en: Fermi Paradox, named after the Italian-American physicist Enrico Fermi.
sentences.zh: 费米悖论，以意大利裔美国物理学家恩里科·费米的名字命名。

sentences.en: Essentially, it asks why, in a universe packed with stars and planets, we have yet to see evidence of life beyond Earth.
sentences.zh: 本质上，它问的是，在一个充满恒星和行星的宇宙中，为什么我们还没有看到地球以外存在生命的证据。

sentences.en: One possible explanation is that life is rare or even unique to Earth.
sentences.zh: 一种可能的解释是，生命是罕见的，甚至是地球独有的。

sentences.en: Another is that intelligent beings exist elsewhere but prefer not to make themselves observable.
sentences.zh: 另一种解释是，智慧生命存在于其他地方，但更愿意不让自己被观察到。

sentences.en: But there is a resolution to the paradox that is more unsettling.
sentences.zh: 但悖论有一个更令人不安的解决方案。

sentences.en: An idea known as the great filter posits that there are difficult, perhaps impassable points in any species' evolution.
sentences.zh: 一个被称为“大过滤器”的想法认为，在任何物种的进化过程中都存在困难的、甚至是无法逾越的关卡。

sentences.en: That filter might kick in early, as complex life begins, or later, when technology produces dangerous rebound effects.
sentences.zh: 那个过滤器可能在早期（当复杂生命开始时）或后期（当技术产生危险的反弹效应时）发挥作用。

sentences.en: Either way, a result would be eerie cosmic silence.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，结果都将是令人毛骨悚然的宇宙寂静。

sentences.en: Rebecca Charbonneau, a science historian at the National Radio Astronomy Observatory who attended
sentences.zh: 国家射电天文台的科学历史学家 Rebecca Charbonneau 参加了

sentences.en: the Penn State Technosignatures Conference, told me that in the mid-1960s, not long after Drake came up with his equation, Carl Sagan, a close friend and colleague of his, asked,
sentences.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州立大学技术签名会议，她告诉我，在 20 世纪 60 年代中期，就在 Drake 提出他的方程后不久，他的密友和同事 Carl Sagan 问道：

sentences.en: Do technical civilizations tend to destroy themselves shortly after they become capable of interstellar radio communications?
sentences.zh: 技术文明是否倾向于在具备星际无线电通信能力后不久就自我毁灭？

sentences.en: Charbonneau says that the specter of nuclear annihilation probably shaped that era's views.
sentences.zh: Charbonneau 说，核毁灭的阴影可能塑造了那个时代的观点。

sentences.en: But while the agents of destruction may have changed, the fear remains.
sentences.zh: 但虽然毁灭的代理人可能已经改变，但恐惧依然存在。

sentences.en: We can glimpse an updated version of how things might end in our warming atmosphere, in our world's shocking declines in biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在变暖的大气层中，在我们世界生物多样性的惊人下降中，瞥见事情可能如何结束的更新版本。

sentences.en: In a sense, this makes the search for technosignatures a search for sustainability as well.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这使得对技术签名的搜索也成为了一场对可持续性的搜索。

sentences.en: Any society that's long lived on geological or astronomical timescales is by definition sustainable, Michael New, the NASA administrator, told me.
sentences.zh: NASA 管理员 Michael New 告诉我，任何在地质或天文时间尺度上长期存在的社会，按定义都是可持续的。

sentences.en: But the fact that a society avoided reducing its impact on the geology and chemistry of its home, he says, might hold a key to how they avoided self-destruction.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，一个社会避免减少其对家园地质和化学影响的事实，可能掌握着他们如何避免自我毁灭的关键。

sentences.en: It may also be that really successful technological societies at some point become hard to detect, he says, because they're living in more or less equilibrium with their planet.
sentences.zh: 他说，这也可能是因为真正成功的技术文明在某种程度上变得难以探测，因为它们与地球处于或多或少的平衡状态中。

sentences.en: This last point is being debated within Frank's group, too.
sentences.zh: 最后这一点在 Frank 的团队内部也在争论。

sentences.en: They don't want to overlook technosignatures because they don't fit ideas of what they should be looking for.
sentences.zh: 他们不想因为技术签名不符合他们应该寻找的想法而忽略它们。

sentences.en: Sophia Sheik gave me an example, the first European settlers to California.
sentences.zh: Sophia Sheik 给了我一个例子，第一批到达加利福尼亚的欧洲定居者。

sentences.en: There are good records, primary sources from the time, that say that they were like, oh, it's like a wonderland out here.
sentences.zh: 有很好的记录，来自当时的原始资料，说他们当时就像是，哦，这里简直是个仙境。

sentences.en: You can just walk through the forest and there's no undergrowth.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接穿过森林，没有灌木丛。

sentences.en: There are just fruit trees growing naturally everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是自然生长的果树。

sentences.en: But what they were seeing was not a natural process.
sentences.zh: 但他们看到的并不是一个自然过程。

sentences.en: It was the result of centuries of tending of the land by indigenous groups.
sentences.zh: 这是土著群体几个世纪以来照料土地的结果。

sentences.en: These were technosignatures, she said, resulting from advanced agricultural techniques that stopped wildfires from breaking out.
sentences.zh: 她说，这些是技术签名，源于先进的农业技术，阻止了野火的爆发。

sentences.en: But Europeans didn't recognize them.
sentences.zh: 但欧洲人没有认出它们。

sentences.en: And so we don't want to see something astronomically and be like, wow, isn't it cool that the universe did that?
sentences.zh: 所以我们不想在天文学上看到一些东西，然后说，哇，宇宙做到了这一点，不是很酷吗？

sentences.en: Just because it doesn't fit our idea of a resource-consuming technological civilization.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为它不符合我们对资源消耗型技术文明的看法。

sentences.en: And yet, it's also possible that years from now, after all the arduous and careful searching, even a total absence of cosmic evidence could prove valuable.
sentences.zh: 然而，也有可能在多年以后，经过所有艰苦而仔细的搜索，即使完全没有宇宙证据也能证明是有价值的。

sentences.en: Two CATS members, Huck Misra and Koparapu, recently considered how the coming age of observations for biosignatures and technosignatures might shed light on the Great Filter.
sentences.zh: 两名 CATS 成员 Huck Misra 和 Koparapu 最近考虑了即将到来的生物签名和技术签名观测时代如何能够阐明“大过滤器”。

sentences.en: If we find biosignatures, that means there's a bunch of planets that can have life on them,
sentences.zh: 如果我们发现了生物签名，那就意味着有一堆行星可以拥有生命，

sentences.en: Huck Misra told me.
sentences.zh: Huck Misra 告诉我。

sentences.en: But if we find plentiful signs of life, but no signs of technology, that's more worrisome.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们发现了丰富的生命迹象，却没有发现技术的迹象，那就更令人担忧了。

sentences.en: It could mean the odds are against technological civilizations sustaining themselves.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着技术文明维持自身生存的几率很小。

sentences.en: They may be exceedingly rare or tend to self-destruct.
sentences.zh: 它们可能极其罕见，或者倾向于自我毁灭。

sentences.en: On the other hand,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，

sentences.en: Huck Misra added, what if we find technosignatures everywhere?
sentences.zh: Huck Misra 补充道，如果我们到处都能找到技术签名呢？

sentences.en: That's actually encouraging.
sentences.zh: 那实际上是令人鼓舞的。

sentences.en: That means that it's possible to have technology in a long-term, sustainable balance with your planet.
sentences.zh: 这意味着有可能在与你的星球保持长期、可持续的平衡中拥有技术。

sentences.en: Would the data, I asked, assuming we ever find it, tell us how to become sustainable or how to remain sustainable?
sentences.zh: 我问，假设我们真的找到了数据，它会告诉我们如何变得可持续或如何保持可持续吗？

sentences.en: No, Huck Misra said, just that it's possible.
sentences.zh: 不，Huck Misra 说，只是说这是可能的。

sentences.en: As for getting there, we would still be on our own.
sentences.zh: 至于如何实现，我们仍然要靠自己。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《The Wirecutter Show》节目中，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让您的客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种一觉睡到天亮的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们需要什么样的光照？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 它们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 它们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 它们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何平台上收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
